question: Does feature-learning richness cause an ordinary two-layer MLP to learn a reusable equality relation rather than a high-sample perceptual shortcut?

key_findings.claim: A four-unit ReLU MLP can implement a compact same-different rule through parallel and antiparallel input-pair weights.
key_findings.evidence: Parallel positive-readout weights make the unequal contribution cancel on identical inputs, while antiparallel negative-readout weights cancel on identical inputs and dominate different inputs when their readout magnitude is large. For Gaussian symbols, the derived different-case success probability tends to one as the negative-to-positive readout ratio grows.

key_findings.claim: Rich and lazy models exhibit sharply different sample and dimension scaling on the synthetic Gaussian-symbol task.
key_findings.evidence: Rich models form near-parallel/antiparallel hidden components, exceed 95% predicted accuracy after roughly five symbols, and remain insensitive to input dimension. In the infinite-width lazy NTK analysis, the stated error upper bound improves as exp(-L/d^2), and simulations require many more symbols as dimension grows.

key_findings.claim: The paper does not actually prove its central rich-ReLU training claim under the experimental model.
key_findings.evidence: The max-margin theorem fixes readouts, replaces ReLU with a quadratic activation, and takes infinite data and symbols. The ReLU result then relies on an independent-walker Markov approximation, mean-field decrement probabilities, self-consistency assumptions, and heuristic independence counts rather than a convergence theorem for gradient descent.

key_findings.claim: The noisy-symbol Bayesian comparison supports population-level generalization but depends on two hand-chosen priors.
key_findings.evidence: Rich models approach the Bayes classifier built from the true Gaussian symbol distribution across noise levels and beat a classifier whose prior is restricted to the finite training symbols. These are diagnostic reference models, not evidence that the trained network represents either posterior internally.

key_findings.claim: Visual results show a useful richness trend, but the tasks retain strong scaffolding and do not demonstrate domain-general equality.
key_findings.evidence: PSVRT and Pentomino use patch-aligned objects and change canvas size mainly by adding empty patches. CIFAR-100 uses frozen ImageNet-pretrained VGG features, reaches roughly 0.6-0.85 rather than near-perfect accuracy, and often performs worse at the richest setting. No cross-task transfer of the learned relation is tested.

key_findings.claim: Richness is a composite parameterization and optimization intervention, so gamma alone is not an isolated causal variable.
key_findings.evidence: Changing gamma rescales the model output and also changes the learning rate as gamma squared times dimension below one and gamma times square-root dimension above one. The derivation targets matched one-step output and relative parameter motion, but there is no control matching optimization trajectories, effective step sizes, or regularization across gamma.

method.core_idea: Interpolate between kernel-like and feature-learning training in one centered MLP, then use representation geometry, sample efficiency, and nuisance robustness as operational signs of perceptual versus conceptual equality behavior.
method.mechanism: Scale the output by gamma and dimension, co-scale SGD, train on pairs made from a restricted symbol set, test on unseen symbols, derive an explicit parallel/antiparallel solution, approximate rich training with max-margin and random-walker arguments, and compare with an infinite-width NTK bound.
assumptions: Parallel/antiparallel first-layer weights are a meaningful operational signature of an equality concept.
The centered gamma parameterization changes representation learning without introducing decisive optimization confounds.
Gaussian symbols and balanced same/different pairs capture the relevant structure of equality learning.
The heuristic independent-walker and self-consistency approximations describe trained wide ReLU MLPs.
Generalization to unseen objects within each constructed task is evidence of relational rather than item-specific learning.

techniques.role: Controls relative feature motion through a centered output and matched learning-rate parameterization.
Uses parallel and antiparallel hidden components as a candidate equality representation.
Characterizes the high-sample, dimension-sensitive lazy limit.
Approximates rich ReLU weight evolution using interacting coordinate-level Markov processes.
Separates train and test object identities to rule out direct item memorization.

evaluations.setting: Noiseless and noisy same-different pairs of Gaussian symbols.
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy on unseen symbols, training-symbol count, input dimension, hidden-weight alignment, and Bayes-reference accuracy.
evaluations.result: Increasing richness greatly improves sample efficiency and dimension robustness; the richest models track the heuristic rich-accuracy curve and the population-prior Bayes benchmark.
evaluations.baseline: Gamma sweep from lazy/NTK-like to rich, plus memorizing and generalizing Bayes classifiers.

evaluations.setting: Patch-aligned PSVRT and rotated Pentomino visual equality.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy on unseen bit patterns or shapes as training variety and canvas width change.
evaluations.result: Richer flattened MLPs need fewer object types and degrade more slowly as empty spatial extent grows.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 category equality with disjoint train/test classes and frozen VGG-16 features.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy versus number of train classes across VGG layers and gamma.
evaluations.result: Moderately rich models generally outperform lazy ones, but performance is far from perfect and the richest setting frequently loses, consistent with overfitting or a non-monotone optimum.
evaluations.baseline: Raw pixels and each intermediate VGG feature layer across gamma.

limitations: The rich-ReLU story is heuristic; its only formal max-margin result changes activation, readout training, and data limits.
The lazy result is an asymptotic NTK upper bound, not a tight finite-width learning law.
Gamma is bundled with output and learning-rate scaling, and no alternative richness intervention is experimentally crossed with it.
Visual nuisance tests use patch alignment and added blank space rather than uncontrolled natural transformations.
CIFAR equality relies on a pretrained VGG representation and does not isolate relation learning from semantic feature quality.
The paper infers a conceptual representation from weight alignment without causal ablation or transfer to a new relation domain.
Speculation about richness in animal brains is not tested and no neural richness measurement is operationalized.
failure_modes: A rich model memorizes idiosyncratic visual features, as the non-monotone CIFAR sweep suggests.
Parallel/antiparallel weights arise from dataset symmetry but fail under transformation, reordered inputs, or a new modality.
Learning-rate changes rather than feature motion explain part of the gamma performance gap.
Unbalanced class or object frequencies let variance and norm cues solve the task without equality.
Pretrained features leak category similarity that makes same-class discrimination easier than true identity reasoning.
The finite-width model departs from both the independent-walker and NTK limits.
reusable_insights: Evaluate relational learning with held-out object identities, nuisance shifts, and representation probes together; any one signal is insufficient.
Separate a representation's geometric signature from causal evidence by removing or transplanting the candidate subspace.
Feature-learning strength can be as important as architecture when a benchmark appears to demand a bespoke reasoning module.
A non-monotone richness sweep is more informative than comparing only a kernel limit with one feature-learning setting.
Claims of abstraction should include cross-domain transfer, not only interpolation across new items drawn from one generator.
open_questions: Can gradient descent on the actual centered ReLU MLP be proved to reach the parallel/antiparallel solution at finite width and sample size?
Do gamma effects persist under matched neural-tangent change, optimizer step, and training time across alternative parameterizations?
Is the aligned hidden subspace causally necessary and sufficient when ablated or transplanted between tasks?
Will a relation learned on synthetic shapes transfer zero-shot to categories, audio, or symbolic sequences?
How does richness interact with explicit relational bottlenecks, Siamese encoders, attention, and object-centric representations?
What measurable neural change in animals would distinguish the proposed rich/perceptual continuum from attention or memory capacity?

competitive_landscape.title: Deep neural networks can learn generalizable same-different visual relations
competitive_landscape.difference: Tartaglini et al. systematically vary ResNet/ViT architecture, pretraining, fine-tuning stimuli, and out-of-distribution object families, obtaining near-perfect transfer in selected CLIP-ViT settings; the reviewed work isolates feature-learning richness in a simpler MLP.

competitive_landscape.title: Visual Reasoning in Object-Centric Deep Neural Networks: A Comparative Cognition Approach
competitive_landscape.difference: Puebla and Bowers test object-centric models across multiple comparative-cognition relations and find persistent hard-case failures; their breadth challenges conclusions drawn from one relation and strongly scaffolded visual tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: When can transformers reason with abstract symbols?
competitive_landscape.difference: Boix-Adsera et al. prove gradient-trained transformers generalize a broad relational-task family under sufficient data and propose a two-parameter head modification, while arguing classical fully connected networks fail in their setup; the reviewed paper obtains an MLP result under a different pair geometry and richness scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: The Relational Bottleneck as an Inductive Bias for Efficient Abstraction
competitive_landscape.difference: The relational-bottleneck program explicitly removes object attributes from the reasoning channel to gain data-efficient abstraction; the reviewed work seeks an emergent relation code in an unconstrained MLP.

competitive_landscape.title: Not-So-CLEVR: Visual Relations Strain Feedforward Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Kim et al. show feedforward CNN and relational-network failures as visual variability grows and motivate attention/memory; the reviewed work argues that a rich optimization regime can reverse such failures in simplified MLP tasks.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Learning richness is the key parameter that moves an MLP along a perceptual-to-conceptual equality-reasoning continuum and may analogously organize biological cognition.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines an explicit equality circuit, rich/lazy asymptotics and heuristics, synthetic symbol splits, noisy Bayes references, three visual tasks, and hidden-weight geometry.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The controlled richness sweep and representation geometry are a valuable bridge between feature-learning theory and cognitive benchmarks. The strongest causal and conceptual language outruns the evidence because the ReLU theory is heuristic, gamma changes multiple training scales, visual tasks are scaffolded, and no cross-domain transfer or causal representation intervention is shown.

reviewer_notes: Read all 29 pages, including every derivation, the max-margin and NTK arguments, walker approximations, Bayes priors, scaling appendix, task configurations, and references. Visually inspected the main synthetic, visual, and all-VGG-layer figures. Primary arXiv and OpenReview competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
